intro: Mining leave lets an underground miner who is close to retirement stop working and still receive most of his pay until he reaches his miners' pension. During the leave he does not go to work at all. He and the employer agree in advance that his contract will end on the day the leave ends, so the leave works as a paid bridge to retirement. It is the main tool the state uses to shrink mine workforces without forced lay-offs.
who_for: An underground employee of a support-system company who was employed there on 1 Jan 2026 and is no more than 5 years away from a pension (counting age and mining service). The leave must end in a pension no later than 31 Dec 2054.
who_excluded: Surface and office staff; anyone who has already used a leave or received earlier restructuring benefits; staff of contractors and private mines.
what_you_get: 80% of monthly pay, calculated like holiday pay (overtime from the last 3 months counts up to 37.5 hours), for up to 5 years, without working.
conditions: The employer must agree; it can be used only once. The leave is lost if the person takes a job at a mine or at a contractor doing mining work, does mining work through his own business, or becomes entitled to a pension.
how_to_apply: Written application to your employer's HR; the employer gets a ZUS certificate and an ARP check. Until 30 Sep 2026 applications had to be on paper.
operator: State budget subsidy paid through the employer.
dates: 1 Jan 2026 – open; active. PGG accepted 2,744 applications; ~1,100 JSW staff on leave
legal_basis: Arts. 11aa, 11ba, 11ca, 11k of the hard-coal mining act (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 520).
take_up: PGG accepted 2,744 applications; about 1,100 JSW staff were already on leave.
known_problems: Early drafts promised 4 years, so information circulating among workers may be out of date; the employer can refuse.

summary.en: Mining leave lets an underground miner who is close to retirement stop working and still receive most of his pay until he reaches his miners' pension. During the leave he does not go to work at all.
summary.pl: Do 5 lat płatnego urlopu (80% wynagrodzenia) bez pracy, jako pomost do emerytury górniczej. Dla pracowników dołowych spółek objętych systemem wsparcia.

name_local: Urlop dla pracowników zakładu przeróbki mechanicznej węgla
intro: This is the same idea as mining leave, but for people who work in the coal-processing plant (where coal is washed and sorted) rather than underground. It is shorter because processing workers reach their pension under different rules.
who_for: Processing-plant employees of a support-system company, employed on 1 Jan 2026, no more than 4 years from a pension; the pension must start by 31 Dec 2053.
what_you_get: 80% of pay for up to 4 years, without working.
conditions: The employer must agree; it can be used only once. The leave is lost if the person takes a job at a mine or at a contractor doing mining work, does mining work through his own business, or becomes entitled to a pension.
how_to_apply: Written application to your employer's HR; the employer gets a ZUS certificate and an ARP check. Until 30 Sep 2026 applications had to be on paper.
operator: State budget subsidy paid through the employer.
take_up: About 224 PGG processing workers were expected to leave on it in July 2026.

summary.en: This is the same idea as mining leave, but for people who work in the coal-processing plant (where coal is washed and sorted) rather than underground. It is shorter because processing workers reach their pension under different rules.
summary.pl: Do 4 lat urlopu z 80% wynagrodzenia przed emeryturą, dla pracowników zakładu przeróbki mechanicznej węgla.

intro: This is a single cash payment for employees who are too far from retirement to get a leave and who agree to leave the company. Unlike the leaves, it is open to everyone on the payroll of a support-system company, including office staff, secretaries and head-office employees. In exchange, the person promises never to return to work in mining.
who_for: Any employee of a support-system company employed on 1 Jan 2026, with at least 3 years' service there, who has no right to a mining or processing leave and is at least 12 months away from a pension.
who_excluded: People with under 3 years' service; people within 12 months of a pension; anyone who already received similar benefits (reported: since 1994); contractor, supplier and private-mine staff.
what_you_get: PLN 170,000, free of income tax and not counted towards health contributions. It can come on top of the ordinary redundancy severance (N05).
conditions: Employer consent; termination by mutual agreement; a signed statement accepting loss or repayment if you return to mining. Mines may not hire, or let contractors use, anyone who took it.
how_to_apply: Written application to HR; ARP checks whether you received similar benefits before.
operator: State budget subsidy paid by the employer.
dates: 1 Jan 2026 – open; active. JSW: 526 paid by 28 May 2026; PGG: 586 in first tranche, up to 738 planned in 2026
status_text: Active since 1 Jan 2026; no closing date in the law.
legal_basis: Art. 11da (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 520); tax exemption in art. 52zd of the PIT Act.
take_up: JSW paid 526 by 28 May 2026; PGG paid 586 in the first tranche and plans up to 738 in 2026.
known_problems: Media say it is also free of social-insurance contributions; the law text read here confirms only the tax and health-contribution points. In the past many workers took severance and later returned to mines, which is why the return ban now exists.

summary.en: This is a single cash payment for employees who are too far from retirement to get a leave and who agree to leave the company. Unlike the leaves, it is open to everyone on the payroll of a support-system company, including office staff, secretaries and head-office employees.
summary.pl: Jednorazowa odprawa 170 000 zł, wolna od podatku dochodowego, dla pracowników spółek objętych systemem wsparcia, którzy dobrowolnie odchodzą z górnictwa.

name_en: Severance when a mine is sold (PLN 120,000 or 12× pay)
intro: When a mining company sells a mine to another company, staff who do not want to move with it can leave with a severance. The amount depends on how soon after the sale they leave.
who_for: Staff of a mine sold under art. 8a; the multiple-of-pay variant is for surface and processing staff with 5+ years.
what_you_get: PLN 120,000 if leaving within 3 months of the sale; or 12, 8 or 4 months' pay depending on timing.
dates: Active, only when a mine is sold
status_text: Active, but only when a mine is actually sold.

summary.en: When a mining company sells a mine to another company, staff who do not want to move with it can leave with a severance. The amount depends on how soon after the sale they leave.
summary.pl: Odprawa przy sprzedaży kopalni: 120 000 zł lub wielokrotność pensji dla osób, które nie przechodzą do nowego właściciela.

name_local: Odprawa z ustawy o zwolnieniach grupowych
intro: Any employer in Poland must pay a severance when it dismisses someone for reasons that are not the employee's fault. Miners get it too, and it is separate from the state-funded PLN 170,000.
who_for: Any employee dismissed in a collective or individual redundancy.
what_you_get: 1 to 3 months' pay depending on length of service; it is taxed.
legal_basis: Act of 13 Mar 2003 on collective redundancies, art. 8.
source_note: [4] · REPORTED (amounts are the standard statutory rule, not re-checked in this research)

summary.en: Any employer in Poland must pay a severance when it dismisses someone for reasons that are not the employee's fault. Miners get it too, and it is separate from the state-funded PLN 170,000.
summary.pl: Ustawowa odprawa przy zwolnieniu z przyczyn niedotyczących pracownika: od 1 do 3 pensji, wypłaca pracodawca.

intro: Some miners receive a monthly equalisation annuity, usually awarded by a court after a work accident or illness. The new law makes sure these payments continue when a mine is liquidated between 2026 and 2049.
who_for: Current and former employees of such mines who hold a court-awarded or settled annuity.
what_you_get: Continued payment of the annuity (details not found)
operator: The mining company from the budget subsidy.
known_problems: The detailed rule was not found in the parts of the act read.

summary.en: Some miners receive a monthly equalisation annuity, usually awarded by a court after a work accident or illness. The new law makes sure these payments continue when a mine is liquidated between 2026 and 2049.
summary.pl: Renta wyrównawcza jest wypłacana dalej także po likwidacji kopalni w latach 2026-2049.

intro: Instead of leaving, a worker from a closing mine can be moved to a mine of another company. His years of service carry over.
who_for: Employees of support-system companies, by agreement between the two employers.
what_you_get: Continued employment and service; no redundancy severance is owed.

summary.en: Instead of leaving, a worker from a closing mine can be moved to a mine of another company. His years of service carry over.
summary.pl: Przeniesienie do kopalni innej spółki z zachowaniem stażu pracy, zamiast odejścia.

intro: Miners can retire much earlier than other workers because underground work is counted as especially hard. The pension is paid by ZUS and uses higher multipliers for mining years.
who_for: Someone with 25 years of full-time underground work (at any age); or aged 55 with 25 years of mining and equivalent work including 10 years of mining work; or aged 50 with 25 years including 15 years of mining work. The person must not be in an open pension fund (OFE) or must have moved those savings to the state.
what_you_get: Pension from ZUS with mining multipliers
how_to_apply: Application to ZUS with employment and mining-work certificates.
legal_basis: Arts. 50a–50e of the Act of 17 Dec 1998 on pensions from the Social Insurance Fund.

summary.en: Miners can retire much earlier than other workers because underground work is counted as especially hard. The pension is paid by ZUS and uses higher multipliers for mining years.
summary.pl: Emerytura górnicza: wcześniejsza emerytura z ZUS dla osób z długim stażem pracy pod ziemią.

name_local: Program wsparcia sektora górnictwa węgla koksującego – świadczenia osłonowe
intro: JSW does not close mines, so it needed a separate government programme to pay its leaving staff the same leave and severance as other companies. The programme runs for six years and is meant to cut JSW's workforce by about a fifth.
who_for: JSW employees meeting the N01–N03 conditions.
what_you_get: Mining leave, processing leave or PLN 170,000 severance.
legal_basis: Council of Ministers Resolution 113 of 28 Apr 2026 (MP 2026 poz. 428).
take_up: About 4,270 departures planned; 526 severances paid by 28 May 2026.

summary.en: JSW does not close mines, so it needed a separate government programme to pay its leaving staff the same leave and severance as other companies. The programme runs for six years and is meant to cut JSW's workforce by about a fifth.
summary.pl: Rządowy program dla JSW na lata 2026-2031: urlopy górnicze i odprawy 170 000 zł dla ok. 4270 odchodzących pracowników.

name_en: Benefits for staff of mines transferred to SRK
intro: From 2015 to 2023, mines being closed were handed to the state company SRK, and their staff could take leave or severance there. No new mines can be handed over after 2023, so this is now a closing, legacy scheme.
who_for: Staff of mines transferred to SRK by 31 Dec 2023.
what_you_get: Mining leave (up to 4 years) or severance (12 months' pay, later PLN 120,000).
dates: 2015 – legacy, no new transfers; 7,650 benefits by May 2017
status_text: 2015 – legacy, no new transfers; 7,650 benefits by May 2017
take_up: 9,022 applications and 7,650 benefits by May 2017, including 4,962 on leave.
known_problems: Without a return ban, some people took severance and went back to mining.

summary.en: From 2015 to 2023, mines being closed were handed to the state company SRK, and their staff could take leave or severance there. No new mines can be handed over after 2023, so this is now a closing, legacy scheme.
summary.pl: Świadczenia dla pracowników kopalń przekazanych do SRK do końca 2023 r. Nowych osób już się nie przyjmuje.

name_local: Ustawa o osłonach socjalnych (energetyka, węgiel brunatny)
name_en: Shield act for power and lignite workers
intro: This is the equivalent package for people in coal power plants and lignite (brown-coal) mines. It matters for mining-related workers whose employer is a power company rather than a hard-coal mine.
who_for: Staff of covered power and lignite companies; leave if at most 4 years from pension, severance if 5+ years' service.
what_you_get: Energy or mining leave up to 4 years at 80% pay, or severance of 12 months' pay; only once.
operator: State budget, up to PLN 1.27bn in 2023–2033.
legal_basis: Dz.U. 2023 poz. 1737, in force since 14 Sep 2023.

summary.en: This is the equivalent package for people in coal power plants and lignite (brown-coal) mines. It matters for mining-related workers whose employer is a power company rather than a hard-coal mine.
summary.pl: Osłony socjalne dla pracowników elektrowni i kopalń węgla brunatnego: urlop do 4 lat albo odprawa 12-krotności pensji.

intro: Workers of the private mine PG Silesia in Czechowice-Dziedzice are not covered by the 2026 benefits, which led to an underground protest. The government's draft UD377 would give them the same benefits, but only if the owner goes bankrupt and the staff are taken over by a state company.
who_for: Staff of private mines, only if the owner goes bankrupt and staff move to a state company
what_you_get: Same benefits as N01–N03
dates: Government adoption planned Q1 2026; current status not found
status_text: Planned; government adoption was scheduled for Q1 2026; current status not found.

summary.en: Workers of the private mine PG Silesia in Czechowice-Dziedzice are not covered by the 2026 benefits, which led to an underground protest. The government's draft UD377 would give them the same benefits, but only if the owner goes bankrupt and the staff are taken over by a state company.
summary.pl: Projekt ustawy UD377: te same świadczenia dla pracowników kopalń prywatnych (PG Silesia), ale tylko po upadłości właściciela.

intro: The agreement between the government, mining unions, mining municipalities and companies sets the timetable for closing thermal-coal mines by 2049. It promises current miners work until retirement or protective benefits instead. It is not a law in itself; the 2025 amendment put much of it into law.
who_for: Miners of state companies
what_you_get: Job guarantees, the basis for mining leave and severance (PLN 120,000 at the time).
dates: Signed 28 May 2021; political agreement, implemented by
status_text: Signed 28 May 2021; political agreement, implemented by
known_problems: Never notified to the European Commission, according to union statements; the energy minister has suggested revising it.

summary.en: The agreement between the government, mining unions, mining municipalities and companies sets the timetable for closing thermal-coal mines by 2049. It promises current miners work until retirement or protective benefits instead.
summary.pl: Umowa społeczna z 2021 r.: harmonogram zamykania kopalń do 2049 r. i gwarancje pracy do emerytury. Nie jest ustawą.

intro: Every county labour office (PUP) offers the standard toolbox for job seekers, open to former miners like anyone else. Since June 2025 you register at the office where you actually live, and age limits on instruments are gone.
who_for: Unemployed and job seekers registered at the PUP of actual residence; no age limits
what_you_get: Job offers and career advice, training, internships, a grant to start a business, a start-up loan, a relocation voucher if you take a job far from home; amounts are set by each office.
how_to_apply: Register as unemployed or a job seeker at your PUP, then apply for each instrument on its form.
legal_basis: Act of 20 Mar 2025 on the labour market and employment services (Dz.U. 2025 poz. 620).

summary.en: Every county labour office (PUP) offers the standard toolbox for job seekers, open to former miners like anyone else. Since June 2025 you register at the office where you actually live, and age limits on instruments are gone.
summary.pl: Powiatowy urząd pracy: oferty pracy, doradztwo, szkolenia, staże, dotacja i pożyczka na firmę, bon na zasiedlenie.

intro: A fund through which employers can get most of the cost of training their staff paid. A firm that hires ex-miners can use it to retrain them.
who_for: Employers, including sole traders; applications in annual PUP calls.
what_you_get: Co-funded courses for staff

summary.en: A fund through which employers can get most of the cost of training their staff paid. A firm that hires ex-miners can use it to retrain them.
summary.pl: Krajowy Fundusz Szkoleniowy: pracodawca może dostać dofinansowanie szkoleń dla swoich pracowników.

intro: Retired miners traditionally received free coal; this is now paid as cash. Its current rules were not researched in this pass.
who_for: Retired former mine and mining-contractor workers
what_you_get: Cash instead of free coal (amount not researched)

summary.en: Retired miners traditionally received free coal; this is now paid as cash. Its current rules were not researched in this pass.
summary.pl: Ekwiwalent pieniężny za węgiel dla emerytów górniczych. Obecne zasady nie zostały sprawdzone.

name_en: Outplacement for mining and mining-related workers (FESL 10.19)
intro: Outplacement is a full package of help for someone who has lost, or is about to lose, a job: a personal plan, retraining and active help finding new work. In Silesia this action gives absolute priority to current and former mining and mining-related workers. Projects can also take in an unemployed family member of a participant.
who_for: People who live or work in the 7 Silesian mining subregions (Bielsko, Bytom, Gliwice, Katowice, Rybnik, Sosnowiec, Tychy) and are at risk of dismissal, planned for dismissal, or were dismissed after 28 May 2021 for reasons not their fault.
who_excluded: People dismissed before 28 May 2021; people outside the 7 subregions.
what_you_get: A career adviser and an individual action plan (always the first step); courses and certification exams, especially green and digital skills; legal and psychological advice; job placement; a subsidised job or equipment for a new workplace; childcare and travel costs; a stipend while training.
how_to_apply: Find a 10.19 project in your area (FE Śląskie project lists, mapadotacji.gov.pl) and fill in its recruitment form.
operator: JTF 90% and state budget 10%; call run by WUP Katowice (ul. Sokolska 29, Katowice; tel. 32 757 33 11; funduszeue@wup-katowice.pl).
dates: Latest call 343/26 ran 30 Apr – 30 Jun 2026 with PLN 177.8m; projects to be chosen in Nov 2026, so recruitment should start in 2027. An earlier call was 146/24.
status_text: Call 343/26: 30 Apr – 30 Jun 2026, PLN 177.8m, decision Nov 2026; earlier call 146/24

summary.en: Outplacement is a full package of help for someone who has lost, or is about to lose, a job: a personal plan, retraining and active help finding new work. In Silesia this action gives absolute priority to current and former mining and mining-related workers.

intro: These projects help people affected by the transition start their own business. Candidates are first assessed by a career adviser, then trained, and after registering a firm they receive a grant they do not have to pay back.
who_for: Same status as R01 (at risk, planned for or dismissed after 28 May 2021) in the 7 subregions; mining and mining-related workers first.
who_excluded: People who already had a registered business before the project; people planning a farm under KRUS; people receiving other start-up grants at the same time.
what_you_get: Business training and advice, then a grant of up to PLN 100,000 per person.
how_to_apply: Recruitment form at a 10.20 project; you will need a business plan that passes the project's review.
dates: Latest call 338/26 ran 27 Feb – 30 Apr 2026; the 2023 call had PLN 124.5m.
status_text: Call 338/26: 27 Feb – 30 Apr 2026; call 074/23 (PLN 124.5m) closed 12 Jan 2024
known_problems: The brief's "PLN 100,000 net" is not in the official text, which gives only a maximum per participant.

summary.en: These projects help people affected by the transition start their own business. Candidates are first assessed by a career adviser, then trained, and after registering a firm they receive a grant they do not have to pay back.
summary.pl: Dotacja do 100 000 zł na założenie firmy, po szkoleniu i ocenie biznesplanu. Ostatni nabór zamknięto 30.04.2026.

intro: Any adult in the mining subregions can get courses, qualifications or studies paid for, choosing them from the national training register (BUR). Many projects give extra points to people from mining.
who_for: Adults who live in the 7 subregions and want to raise their skills on their own initiative; some projects prioritise mining workers who left after 1 Jan 2021, people 55+ and the unemployed.
what_you_get: Funded training, studies or exam fees.
how_to_apply: Join a 10.17 project operator in your subregion, then book courses in BUR.

intro: This is the only regional action that names families of mining workers directly. Mining municipalities run local projects that strengthen communities going through mine closures: social activities, debates and mediation, and work on mining heritage.
who_for: Residents of mining municipalities, including families of mining and mining-related workers.
what_you_get: Depends on the gmina's project (activities, support, events).
how_to_apply: Ask your gmina or social-assistance centre whether it runs a 10.24 project.
dates: First call closed 20 Nov 2023; a new call for mining municipalities was announced on 15 Dec 2025. Total action budget PLN 200.3m.
status_text: Call 024/23 (rolling, closed 20 Nov 2023); new call for mining municipalities announced 15 Dec 2025

summary.en: This is the only regional action that names families of mining workers directly. Mining municipalities run local projects that strengthen communities going through mine closures: social activities, debates and mediation, and work on mining heritage.

who_for: Staff of social-assistance and public employment service institutions in the 7 subregions (WUP itself excluded).
what_you_get: Courses, postgraduate studies, study visits, advisory and legal services.

summary.en: Despite its name, this action is not for miners. It trains the people who help miners: staff of social-assistance centres and labour offices, so they can give better advice and work together across institutions.

intro: PGG, the regional rail operator Koleje Śląskie and the service firm Synercom signed an agreement to move miners leaving PGG into railway jobs. Participants get career advice and aptitude tests, are trained for a rail trade and are helped through recruitment, with the option of a subsidised first job. intro: This is the one-off payment OKD makes to every core employee whose job ends because the mine is closing. OKD and the miners' unions agreed it in 2022 so that people leaving early and those kept for the liquidation are treated the same way. The amount depends on years of service: the Czech Labour Code sets a lower minimum, and OKD's collective agreement and Social Programme raise it. OKD set aside CZK 1.3 billion for it from the reserve it built up in 2022–2024.
who_for: OKD core employees dismissed or leaving by agreement for organisational reasons. Contractor staff working in the mine are paid under their own employer's terms, not this one.
what_you_get: 4× average monthly pay after at least 1 year of service, rising to 11× after 16 or more years. The 150 people who left in August 2025 had worked an average of 29 years and received 11×. The ~900 who left in January–February 2026 received over CZK 0.5 million each on average.

funder: OKD reserve (state-owned via Prisko); CZK 1.3 bn
dates: Agreed with unions in 2022; paid in each wave 2025–2026
legal_basis: Collective agreement + OKD Social Programme; Labour Code §67 (minimum)
known_problems: Severance is taxed as income but carries no social or health insurance, so the months it covers do not add to the pension record. Since 2024 it no longer delays unemployment benefit.

summary.en: This is the one-off payment OKD makes to every core employee whose job ends because the mine is closing. OKD and the miners' unions agreed it in 2022 so that people leaving early and those kept for the liquidation are treated the same way.

Consultants also help with CVs, cover letters, interview preparation, finding vacancies, dealing with the Labour Office, retraining choices and starting a business. Offices opened at every mine during earlier closures and reopened in May 2025 for the ČSM closure.
who_for: Any OKD employee who is about to leave, or who left no more than 6 months ago. People who have reached pension age are not included. Contractor staff: not stated.

operator: OKD HR specialists; offices at the mine; contacts not published online
known_problems: The 6-month window after leaving is strict. Results for 2025–2026 have not been published.

name_local: Příspěvek ke zmírnění sociálních dopadů (NV 167/2016 Sb.)
intro: This is a monthly state payment that bridges the period after a mine job ends, until the person finds new work or reaches pension age. The government created it in May 2016 when OKD was insolvent; it lapsed when the insolvency ended in 2018 and was restored for OKD leavers in October 2020. The Ministry of Industry and Trade (MPO) pays it from the state budget, and the state enterprise Diamo receives and checks applications. The payment is longer for older workers with long service, who are the least likely to find new jobs.
who_for: OKD employees (and the Diamo branch that took over OKD staff) whose job ended by notice or agreement for organisational reasons, after at least 2 years of continuous employment. The region's unemployment rate must have been at or above the national average in the previous half-year, which applies to Karviná.
what_you_get: CZK 8,000 a month if you mainly worked underground, CZK 5,300 if you mainly worked on the surface. Duration: 3 months with under 5 years' service; with 5+ years, 6 months plus 3 months per additional full year, up to 36 months. Underground workers aged 50+ with 25 years' service and 3,300 underground shifts, and surface workers aged 55+ with 25 years' service, get 60 months.
how_to_apply: Fill in the form in Annex 2 of the regulation and submit it through Diamo within 6 months of the end of employment. Diamo forwards it to MPO within 10 days; payments start the month after approval and are paid monthly in arrears.
operator: Diamo social centre (úsek ODRA, Sirotčí, Ostrava-Vítkovice – reported 2017); decision by MPO
funder: State budget, Ministry of Industry and Trade (MPO); cost estimate up to CZK 820 m (2020–2031)
territory: Region where unemployment is ≥ national average
take_up: 1,340 applicants, CZK 236.4 m paid by early 2020; 1,296 applicants by Jun 2021
known_problems: The right expires if you miss the 6-month deadline. Payment stops when an old-age pension starts. A special miners' allowance (P10) or compensation for lost earnings is deducted. No 2026 source confirms that ČSM leavers are being paid.

name_local: Snížený důchodový věk horníků (§37b–37c z. 155/1995 Sb.)
name_en: Reduced retirement age for deep miners
intro: Underground work in deep mines is recognised as too hard to do until the standard pension age. Since a 2016 amendment, a deep miner who has worked enough shifts underground can retire 7 years earlier than the general pension age, without any reduction of the pension. Women in this group are treated the same as men of the same birth date.
who_for: People who started working underground in a deep mine before 1 October 2016 and worked at least 3,300 underground shifts in coal (2,200 in uranium). Lower limits apply if they had to stop after reaching the maximum permitted exposure. A shift counts if most of it was spent underground.
what_you_get: Old-age pension 7 years before your standard retirement age, at full amount.
how_to_apply: Claim the pension at ČSSZ or the district social security office (OSSZ). The employer confirms the shifts; your recorded risk shifts are shown in the pension account statement on the ČSSZ ePortál.
legal_basis: Act 155/1995 Sb. §37b–37c; NV 363/2009 Sb. for older cases
known_problems: Surface workers do not qualify, nor do people who started underground after 1 October 2016.

summary.en: Underground work in deep mines is recognised as too hard to do until the standard pension age. Since a 2016 amendment, a deep miner who has worked enough shifts underground can retire 7 years earlier than the general pension age, without any reduction of the pension.

intro: Outplacement II is a Labour Office project for people who are about to lose their job in a mass layoff, so that they move "from work to work" without a long gap. It also pays employers who take on such people. It runs nationwide from July 2024 to October 2028 and is funded by the EU (ESF+) and the Czech state.
who_for: Employees in collective redundancy or in their notice period; those likely to leave within 6 months (by agreement or end of a fixed-term contract); employees of firms switching to a new business programme; and new employers hiring them.
what_you_get: Individual and group counselling; skills diagnostics; retraining and professional qualifications; job placement; refund of travel costs and of the medical entry examination; childcare or care for a dependant in justified cases. A new employer can receive up to CZK 15,000 a month for 9 months towards the person's wage. The current employer can get wage support while the employee retrains.
how_to_apply: Register at the Labour Office as an interested person (zájemce o zaměstnání), then attend an entry interview where you sign the project documents. Free call centre: 800 77 99 00.
funder: ESF+ (OPZ+) + state budget; reg. no. CZ.03.01.03/00/22_041/0004600
known_problems: Registration is required. The earlier phase involved 2,103 people.

summary.en: Outplacement II is a Labour Office project for people who are about to lose their job in a mass layoff, so that they move "from work to work" without a long gap. It also pays employers who take on such people.
summary.cs: Outplacement II Úřadu práce: poradenství, rekvalifikace, zprostředkování práce a příspěvek novému zaměstnavateli. Běží do 31. 10. 2028.

name_local: Mobilní pracoviště ÚP v areálu Dolu ČSM
name_en: Labour Office mobile workplace at ČSM
intro: From 2025, Labour Office advisers worked directly on the ČSM site, so miners could stop by on the way to their shift instead of travelling to Havířov or Karviná. They explain how to register correctly, how to claim unemployment benefit and what retraining is available. They also help with CVs and interview preparation and show vacancies in the region. OKD's April 2026 newsletter still mentions the mobile workplace alongside Nová šichta.
who_for: OKD employees affected by the mass layoff.
what_you_get: Advice on the spot.
how_to_apply: Walk in; opening hours not published.
known_problems: Exact opening dates and hours not published

intro: These are the Labour Office's standard ways to help any job seeker back into work, available alongside Outplacement II. In the Moravian-Silesian Region the most requested retraining courses for miners have been driving licences (groups C, D and T and professional licences), social-care work, welding and accounting.
who_for: People registered at the Labour Office as job seekers or interested persons.
what_you_get: Retraining paid by the Labour Office; a "self-chosen" retraining (zvolená rekvalifikace) where you pick the course; wage subsidies to employers for socially useful jobs (SÚPM); public works (VPP); and an induction contribution for employers. In 2021 the region spent CZK 17.9 million on retraining for 874 + 941 people.
how_to_apply: Register at a Labour Office contact point (Karviná, Havířov, Orlová, Bohumín, Frýdek-Místek and others) and agree a plan with your adviser.
operator: Labour Office branches (Karviná, Havířov, Orlová, Bohumín, Frýdek-Místek, Most, Sokolov...)
take_up: Moravian-Silesian Region 2021: 874 + 941 in retraining, CZK 17.9 m
known_problems: These tools are discretionary, not an entitlement.

summary.en: These are the Labour Office's standard ways to help any job seeker back into work, available alongside Outplacement II. In the Moravian-Silesian Region the most requested retraining courses for miners have been driving licences (groups C, D and T and professional licences), social-care work, welding and accounting.

what_you_get: Course costs and wage costs during training
how_to_apply: Employer applies

intro: Anyone who registers at the Labour Office and meets the insurance conditions receives unemployment benefit. Under the 2026 rules the benefit is higher in the first two months (reported up to 80% of net earnings) and then falls. Since 2024 it has been paid from the first month even when severance was paid; before that, severance pushed the start back. Registration also means the state pays the person's health insurance.
who_for: Registered job seekers
what_you_get: Higher benefit in first months (2026 rules); paid from month 1 even with severance (since 2024)
how_to_apply: Register as a job seeker at the Labour Office.
known_problems: People who do not register must pay their own health insurance, and the period may not count towards the pension.

summary.en: Anyone who registers at the Labour Office and meets the insurance conditions receives unemployment benefit. Under the 2026 rules the benefit is higher in the first two months (reported up to 80% of net earnings) and then falls.
summary.cs: Podpora v nezaměstnanosti se vyplácí od prvního měsíce i při odstupném. Po registraci platí zdravotní pojištění stát.

intro: OPST is the Czech programme of the EU Just Transition Fund, made to soften the end of coal in the three most affected regions: Moravian-Silesian, Ústí and Karlovy Vary. The Ministry of the Environment manages it with the State Environmental Fund (SFŽP); each region has its own share (CZK 17.4 billion for Moravian-Silesian) and helps design calls. The money goes mainly to firms, towns, schools, universities and NGOs through calls in seven themes, including business, research, new energy, land restoration and "people and skills". Individual miners benefit indirectly: through new jobs, training projects run by employers or schools, TRAUTOM (P17) and business loans (P19).
who_for: Organisations in the three regions; individuals only as self-employed applicants in some calls.
what_you_get: Grants, vouchers and interest-free loans, depending on the call.
how_to_apply: Through calls listed on opst.cz and the regional sites (hrajemskrajem.msk.cz for Moravian-Silesian). Many calls go first to the region, which then opens its own call for end applicants months later.
operator: Ministry of the Environment (MZP); SFZP; spravedlivatransformace@mzp.cz
funder: Just Transition Fund (JTF) + state; CZK 39–42.7 bn (sources differ)
known_problems: Sources give different totals (CZK 39.4–42.7 billion). Several calls closed on 30 April 2026.

summary.en: OPST is the Czech programme of the EU Just Transition Fund, made to soften the end of coal in the three most affected regions: Moravian-Silesian, Ústí and Karlovy Vary. The Ministry of the Environment manages it with the State Environmental Fund (SFŽP); each region has its own share (CZK 17.4 billion for Moravian-Silesian) and helps design calls.
summary.cs: Operační program Spravedlivá transformace: granty a úvěry pro firmy, obce, školy a neziskovky v uhelných krajích.

intro: TRAUTOM is the Moravian-Silesian Region's strategic project for adult education during the transition. It is run by the Moravian-Silesian Employment Pact (MS Pakt zaměstnanosti) with VŠB – Technical University of Ostrava and the Moravian-Silesian Automotive Cluster. It differs from school projects by targeting adults. It offers three kinds of services: analyses of the labour market, services for citizens, and services for firms. For citizens it provides group and individual activities for people who need to change jobs and helps them choose retraining or further education. For firms it prepares training plans and helps them apply for OPST money (P18) free of charge.
who_for: Adults in the Moravian-Silesian Region who want or need to change work; firms in the region.
what_you_get: Free career counselling and guidance on retraining; for firms, free help with grant applications.
how_to_apply: Contact MS Pakt (Varenská 1414/1, Ostrava) through trautom.cz, or through your employer.
operator: Moravskoslezský pakt zaměstnanosti, Varenská 1414/1, Ostrava; trautom.cz
known_problems: No figures on how many ex-miners used it were found.

summary.en: TRAUTOM is the Moravian-Silesian Region's strategic project for adult education during the transition. It is run by the Moravian-Silesian Employment Pact (MS Pakt zaměstnanosti) with VŠB – Technical University of Ostrava and the Moravian-Silesian Automotive Cluster.
summary.cs: TRAUTOM: bezplatné kariérní poradenství a pomoc s výběrem rekvalifikace pro dospělé v Moravskoslezském kraji.

intro: This call funds firms in the coal regions that train or retrain their staff for new fields, for example technical skills, IT and languages. A single project can receive up to EUR 2 million, and the TRAUTOM team helps firms prepare it.
who_for: Employers, not individuals; ex-miners benefit if their new employer uses it.
what_you_get: Up to EUR 2 million per project
how_to_apply: Firm applies with help from TRAUTOM
status_text: Whether the call is still open was not confirmed.

summary.en: This call funds firms in the coal regions that train or retrain their staff for new fields, for example technical skills, IT and languages. A single project can receive up to EUR 2 million, and the TRAUTOM team helps firms prepare it.

intro: This is an interest-free, fee-free investment loan from the state Národní rozvojová banka, funded by OPST, for small and medium businesses and self-employed people in the three coal regions. It pays for long-term assets such as machines, equipment and software. It is the main route for an ex-miner who wants to start or expand a business, for example a workshop.
who_for: SMEs and self-employed people with a project in the Moravian-Silesian, Ústí or Karlovy Vary Region.
what_you_get: CZK 0.5–100 million in Moravian-Silesian (up to CZK 60 million elsewhere), covering up to 90% of eligible costs, at 0% interest.
how_to_apply: Online application to NRB (info line 255 721 111, info@nrb.cz), by 31 December 2026.
funder: JTF via NRB; CZK 3.335 bn (MSK CZK 1.915 bn)
known_problems: The minimum loan is CZK 0.5 million, and own or bank funds are needed, so it does not suit very small start-ups. No grant scheme aimed at miners starting a business was found.

summary.en: This is an interest-free, fee-free investment loan from the state Národní rozvojová banka, funded by OPST, for small and medium businesses and self-employed people in the three coal regions. It pays for long-term assets such as machines, equipment and software.
summary.cs: Úvěr Transformace: bezúročný úvěr 0,5 až 100 mil. Kč pro malé firmy a OSVČ v uhelných krajích. Žádosti do 31. 12. 2026.

intro: The Moravian-Silesian Region started this project to stop people moving away from Havířov, Karviná and Orlová. Eligible people get a free 365-day ODISka public-transport card for commuting to work and to Ostrava. The regional development agency ARR handles applications and issues the cards.
who_for: Employed people with permanent residence in Havířov, Karviná or Orlová who either moved there after the project was announced or are school or university graduates.
what_you_get: Free 365-day ODISka transport card
how_to_apply: Application to ARR (mobilita@arr.cz) with an employer's confirmation.
known_problems: It was not designed for ex-miners who already live there, and its current status was not found.

summary.en: The Moravian-Silesian Region started this project to stop people moving away from Havířov, Karviná and Orlová. Eligible people get a free 365-day ODISka public-transport card for commuting to work and to Ostrava.
summary.cs: Zaměstnanecká mobilita: bezplatná roční ODISka pro dojíždění za prací (Havířov, Karviná, Orlová). Pravidla z roku 2017.

intro: RE:START is the government's long-term strategy for the economic restructuring of the three coal regions, run by the Ministry for Regional Development since 2017. It works through action plans (the 6th covers 2025–2026) that steer national and EU money towards these regions, for example by reserving calls or giving extra points to projects there. It was the basis for the OPST plan. Projects worth about CZK 10 billion were supported through it by the early 2020s.
who_for: The three coal regions
what_you_get: No direct benefit; it shapes which calls and investments reach the regions.
how_to_apply: Not for individuals
known_problems: No direct help to workers

summary.en: RE:START is the government's long-term strategy for the economic restructuring of the three coal regions, run by the Ministry for Regional Development since 2017. It works through action plans (the 6th covers 2025–2026) that steer national and EU money towards these regions, for example by reserving calls or giving extra points to projects there.
summary.cs: Strategie RE:START: státní koordinace podpory uhelných regionů. Bez přímé pomoci lidem.

intro: REFRESH is the largest research project in VŠB-TUO's history: CZK 2.5 billion from OPST, built on four "living labs" shared with the University of Ostrava. Its social part, led by Dr Dana Vicherková at the Faculty of Education, studies how the transition affects families of OKD and supplier workers. Researchers interview miners and their children aged 6–24 about education paths, retraining options and the barriers that stop people from further education. A separate strand records stories of former miners and metalworkers and how they coped with the change.
who_for: Families of OKD and supplier staff (research participants)
what_you_get: No direct service. It is a source of evidence for the hub, and families can take part as interviewees.
how_to_apply: Research participation
operator: University of Ostrava, Faculty of Education
known_problems: Research only

summary.en: REFRESH is the largest research project in VŠB-TUO's history: CZK 2.5 billion from OPST, built on four "living labs" shared with the University of Ostrava. Its social part, led by Dr Dana Vicherková at the Faculty of Education, studies how the transition affects families of OKD and supplier workers.
summary.cs: REFRESH: výzkum Ostravské univerzity o rodinách horníků a překážkách v rekvalifikaci. Rodiny se mohou zapojit jako respondenti.

intro: Under a Recovery Plan project (March 2024 – December 2025, CZK 38.2 million), VŠB-TUO created five new reskilling courses. They cover ESG and modern management, pilot training for sustainable aviation, circular audit, smart infrastructure and energy geotechnics. The energy geotechnics course ran free of charge in the winter semester 2025/26 for up to 15 participants.
who_for: Adults (not miner-specific)
what_you_get: The courses were open to adults but not aimed at miners, and the funded run has ended. An earlier VŠB-TUO programming course for miners ("Razíme cestu", 2017) is described in the history section.
how_to_apply: Online application
funder: Czech Recovery Plan (NPO), CZK 38.2 m (whole project)
known_problems: Not targeted at miners

intro: Sokolovská uhelná, the brown-coal miner near Sokolov, has been shrinking since 2020. About 700 people left in 2020 when the Vřesová plant closed; they received severance under the collective agreement and the state allowance (P07). The firm also tried to move people to its subsidiaries, now grouped as SUAS Group. Around 90 people left at the turn of 2025 and about 120 more in 2026, with the conditions of the current collective agreement kept.
who_for: Sokolovská uhelná employees made redundant.
what_you_get: Severance per the collective agreement (amounts not published), plus P07.
how_to_apply: Through the employer.
known_problems: The group is loss-making, so the subsidiaries cannot absorb everyone.

summary.en: Sokolovská uhelná, the brown-coal miner near Sokolov, has been shrinking since 2020. About 700 people left in 2020 when the Vřesová plant closed; they received severance under the collective agreement and the state allowance (P07).
summary.cs: Odstupné podle kolektivní smlouvy Sokolovské uhelné, plus státní příspěvek a přesuny do dceřiných firem.

intro: Nadace OKD is OKD's foundation. It funds public projects in towns affected by mining. In 2024 its board chose 7 projects worth CZK 20.1 million. They include a refurbished ceremony hall in Doubrava, a playground and workout area in Havířov's Stromovka park, new playground equipment in Horní Suchá, a brine inhalatorium in Karviná and sports facilities in Orlová. It does not support individual miners, and it is not the "Nadace Nová šichta" mentioned in the brief.
who_for: Municipalities only, not individuals; 2024 round went to Doubrava, Havířov, Horní Suchá, Karviná, Orlová, Petrovice u Karviné and Stonava
operator: Nadace OKD; CZK 20.1 m for 7 projects (2024)
dates: 2024 round reported; future rounds not found
status_text: 2024 round reported; future rounds not found

summary.en: Nadace OKD is OKD's foundation. It funds public projects in towns affected by mining.

name_local: Sociální služby na dlani / Den pro pečující
intro: The Social Department of Karviná City Hall runs this programme to show residents what social services exist. It added a "Day for carers" event offering practical help, counselling and sharing of experience for people caring for relatives at home. It is open to all residents, so miners' families can use it, but it is not aimed at them.
who_for: All residents, including miners' families

name_en: EURES: European job mobility portal and advisers
intro: EURES is the EU's job mobility network. Its portal lists vacancies across the EU, including Poland and Czechia, and EURES advisers at labour offices help people who want to work across the border.
who_for: Anyone looking for work in another EU country, including cross-border commuters between Czechia and Poland.
what_you_get: Job vacancies, a CV database employers can search, and free advice from EURES advisers at labour offices.
how_to_apply: Create an account on eures.europa.eu, or ask for a EURES adviser at your labour office (Úřad práce or PUP/WUP).
operator: European Labour Authority; national labour offices
evidence_note: REPORTED (from a separate web search, not part of the two research databases)

summary.en: The EU job portal and EURES advisers help people find work across the border between Poland and Czechia.
summary.cs: Evropský portál práce EURES a poradci EURES na úřadech práce pomáhají najít práci za hranicí, v Polsku i v Česku.
